nodes.title: Reliable first-day Assura adoption
nodes.description: Deliver the evidence-backed first-day adoption and targeted-coverage fixes with per-item acceptance; the core-performance research spike is independent. This does not certify external retention, native owner acceptance or a public release.

nodes.title: Expose configured nonblocking violations in Review and finding history
nodes.description:
Both real projects retain advisory=0 while Check names low findings; 501 to 700 lines produces no new/worsened Review finding. Assura has 13 nonblocking findings, but two optional baseline folders dominate actions.

Acceptance:
- A passing explicit low max_lines fixture emits a bounded named advisory and new/worsened/resolved history.
- Keep Review exit 0, Check severity exits, stable fingerprints, and honest overflow totals.
- Rank actionable configured violations ahead of optional setup suggestions.

Evidence: typescript-trial.md: baseline-mutation-review, python-trial.md: worsened-review, src/cli/project_review/report.rs:58-59
Related existing work: R07, A06
Priority rationale: Missing configured findings undermines working feedback, irrespective of command speed.
Source: f3540d4a11d36afa43f69c96fd7f1c233599822a; v0.4.1. No implementation authorized by this review.

nodes.title: Preserve established agent policy when merging onboarding baseline
nodes.description:
Onboarding closes .agents and rejects existing .agents/project-policy.json; the same conflict appears on Assura own README.md. Bytes survive but policy intent conflicts before specialization. Assura self-onboarding also introduces inherited PascalCase errors in existing docs.

Acceptance:
- Reproduce existing .agents files and custom skill conventions in a disposable existing-project fixture.
- Preserve owner policy and deliberate closures; report unresolved merge constraints without adding an incompatible passing claim.
- Original files/hooks remain unchanged, repeated onboarding is idempotent, and generated policy passes or reports an actionable conflict.

Evidence: python-trial.md: onboard-first and onboard-baseline-check, self-onboard.json, self-doctor-after-onboard.json
Related existing work: A02, A03
Priority rationale: Setup can impose a failing policy on existing agent infrastructure.
Source: f3540d4a11d36afa43f69c96fd7f1c233599822a; v0.4.1. No implementation authorized by this review.

nodes.title: Detect when installation leaves an older Assura first on PATH
nodes.description:
Native public installer passes checksum and reports success, but when old /usr/local/bin precedes the destination already on PATH, command -v assura still selects 0.4.0 after installing 0.4.1. No warning is printed in that case.

Acceptance:
- Seed old and new bin directories with old first and both present on PATH.
- Report the installed version and actual command resolution; if shadowed, provide a concrete correction without editing shell files or replacing another install.
- Verify both companions and a fresh-shell version canary after the documented correction.

nodes.title: Make targeted captured-relationship checks correct and explicit
nodes.description:
Full Check rejects missing Button.test.tsx; explicit Check of Button.tsx returns exit0 with no relationship finding. Relationship traversal skips its selected root entry even when it is a file. Prepared changed-path checking separately full-falls-back, so this does not establish a cache/session defect.

Acceptance:
- Define the supported ordinary file-target relationship contract before changing behavior; distinguish it from explicit LS-Lint target semantics and whole-project coverage.
- A selected captured producer with a missing counterpart/provider must not silently disappear: enforce its required relation or explicitly report that check as omitted with a full-project follow-up.
- Prove full/file/directory, provided/missing counterpart, producer deletion, configuration changes, cache and prepared fallback cases with exact findings and exits.
- Retain presence-versus-behavior semantics: an existing test filename does not prove a test executed or is adequate.

Evidence: core-capability-probe.json, raw capability-pass/transcript.json: missing-test-full and missing-test-file-target, systemic-filesystem-review.md: P4, src/cli/check/custom_constraints.rs:330-334
Related existing work: A03, R01, A06
Priority rationale: Core policy coverage must remain trustworthy before claiming cheaper scoped or incremental checks.
Source: f3540d4a11d36afa43f69c96fd7f1c233599822a; v0.4.1. No implementation authorized by this review.

nodes.title: Attribute core filesystem work and select one systemic optimization
nodes.description:
Rich full-engine checks eagerly fetch metadata without a size limit, independently walk overlapping scopes, and scan all scopes per uncached directory. Existing static fast-path indexes and prepared reuse already exist. No current wall-time fraction or causal speedup is established.

Acceptance:
- Profile ordinary public check with a source/binary/policy-bound rich repository and controlled wide-tree case; count stat-family calls, directory enumerations, reads/bytes, allocations or peak RSS, CPU and wall time by consumer.
- First discriminate no-size-policy eager metadata; then attribute identical-scope test/lifecycle enumeration. Preserve a naming-only negative control and full result/exit equivalence.
- Produce one smallest supported keep/defer decision; do not implement a shared inventory, index rewrite, daemon, new entrypoint or parallel traversal merely because source work is repeated.
- For any later performance candidate, use uninstrumented balanced same-host before/after public-command samples, exact quiet comparison, existing keep/stop criteria, accepted-fixture spillover and unchanged no-slower/native/warm gates.
- Keep literal/glob scope indexing conditional on measured dominance. Incremental eligibility expansion additionally requires NU13 coverage resolution and deletion/rename/provider/config invalidation proof; source review alone proves no gain.

Evidence: systemic-filesystem-review.md, systemic-performance-hypotheses.json, src/cli/check/file_limits.rs:19-25, src/cli/check/test_relationship.rs:18-19, src/cli/check/rule_plan.rs:58-82
Related existing work: R02, R03, R01, CF01, CF03, CF04
Priority rationale: Explicit user focus on systemic filesystem performance; one investigation, not four speculative implementation cards.
Source: f3540d4a11d36afa43f69c96fd7f1c233599822a; v0.4.1. No implementation authorized by this review.
